intro.html: Things grow and things shrink. Gardens flourish, towns burgeon and rabbits proliferate; the moon wanes, the tide ebbs and storms abate. Each word tells you not just which way something is going but how: fast or slow, by multiplying, by sinking, by wasting away.

Growing: flourish and thrive (grow strong and healthy), burgeon (grow fast), proliferate (multiply). Shrinking or easing: wane and dwindle (little by little), ebb (flow back like the tide), abate (lessen; storms, noise, pain), subside (die down or sink lower) and atrophy (waste away from lack of use).

words.def: to grow well and healthily; to do very well
words.ex: Tomatoes {flourish} in Nana Lou’s sunny backyard.
words.ctx: The little bakery {flourished} after the newspaper praised its bread; within a year it had doubled its staff and opened a second shop across town.
words.etym: From Old French florir, from Latin florere, “to bloom,” from flos, “flower.”

mn.text: Nana Lou’s garden bursts with flowers of every color, taller and brighter every week. It {flourishes}.

scene.alt: A grandmother cheers beside a row of tall, bright flowers blooming in her garden.

words.def: to grow strong and healthy; to do well
words.ex: The rescued puppy {thrived} on long walks and lots of attention.
words.ctx: Some plants wilt in deep shade, but ferns {thrive} there; they grow thick and green under the tall trees where little else will grow.
words.etym: From Old Norse thrifask, “to grasp for oneself, to prosper.”

mn.cue: THRIVE rhymes with HIVE: a busy, growing HIVE
mn.text: Every week there are more bees and more honey; the busy hive grows and grows. It {thrives}!

scene.alt: A girl holds up a jar of honey beside a busy, growing beehive with happy bees.

words.ex: Weeds {burgeoned} in the empty lot after a week of rain.
words.ctx: The town’s population {burgeoned} after the new factory opened; in just three years, two new schools were built and the old one doubled in size.

mn.cue: BURGER-on: the BURGER stack grows FAST
mn.text: At the cookout, Sven’s stack of burgers grows fast: one, then three, then six, taller than his nose! The stack {burgeons}.

scene.alt: A laughing cook stands beside a towering stack of burgers that keeps growing.

words.def: to increase quickly in number; to multiply
words.ex: Rabbits {proliferated} in the meadow until there were hundreds.
words.ctx: Food trucks have {proliferated} downtown; five years ago there were two, and now dozens line every street at lunchtime.
words.etym: From proliferation, from French prolifère, “bearing offspring,” from Latin proles (offspring) + ferre (to bear).

mn.cue: PROLIFIC bunnies: LIFE makes more LIFE
mn.text: Two rabbits in spring, twenty by summer, two hundred by fall! The rabbits {proliferate}.

scene.alt: A farm field fills with more and more rabbits while a woman stares in shock.

words.def: to grow smaller or weaker little by little
words.ex: Interest in the new game {waned} after a few weeks.
words.ctx: The moon waxes for two weeks and then {wanes}, shrinking a little each night until only a thin sliver is left.

mn.cue: WANE: a little LESS each night
mn.text: Each night Pip looks out his window, and each night the moon is a little thinner. The moon {wanes}.

scene.alt: A boy at night points at a row of moons that grow smaller from Monday to Thursday.

words.def: to grow smaller little by little until little is left
words.ex: Our supply of marshmallows {dwindled} as the campfire night went on.
words.ctx: As the afternoon wore on, the crowd at the parade {dwindled}; by five o’clock, only a few families were left, folding up their chairs.
words.etym: From dwine, an old word meaning “to waste away,” from Old English dwinan.

mn.cue: DWIN-DLE like a CAN-DLE: it shrinks down
mn.text: Maya reads late into the night, and her candle shrinks from tall to short to a tiny stub. It {dwindles}.

scene.alt: A sleepy teen reads beside three candles that shrink from tall to a tiny stub.

words.def: to flow back out, like the tide; to fade away
words.ex: As the tide {ebbed}, the children hunted for crabs in the pools left behind.
words.ctx: Her anger {ebbed} slowly as she listened to her brother’s apology, and by the end she was laughing.

mn.cue: EBB: the sea slides BACK, back, back
mn.text: The water slides back out to sea, and Sami finds starfish and shells left behind on the wet sand. The tide {ebbs}.

labels.text: EBB: the tide goes BACK OUT

scene.alt: At low tide, a boy kneels on the wet sand collecting starfish and shells the sea left behind.

words.def: to become less strong or intense
words.ex: We waited inside the barn until the storm {abated}.
words.ctx: The noise from the street party finally {abated} after midnight, and the tired family could at last fall asleep.
words.etym: From Old French abatre, “to beat down,” from batre, “to beat.”
words.note: Abate is used for storms, noise, pain and anger that ease.

mn.cue: A-BAIT: the storm calms, so out comes the BAIT
mn.text: The wind drops, the rain slows, and the sun peeks out. The storm {abates}, so Omar grabs his bait and heads back to fishing.

scene.alt: A fisherman cheers on the dock as the storm eases and the sun comes out.

words.def: to die down; also, to sink to a lower level
words.ex: After the river flooded, it took a week for the water to {subside}.
words.ctx: Kai’s giggles finally {subsided} when the teacher glanced his way, though they came right back the moment she turned to the board.
words.etym: From Latin subsidere, “to settle down, to sink”: sub (under, down) + sidere (to settle).

mn.text: After the flood, the water in the park sinks down, lower and lower, until the bench appears again. The flood {subsides}.

scene.alt: A girl in a raincoat points as floodwater in the park sinks back down, uncovering a bench.

words.def: to waste away or weaken from lack of use
words.ex: After six weeks in a cast, the muscles in Dev’s arm had begun to {atrophy}.
words.ctx: Skills you never practice can {atrophy}; after ten years without playing, Grandma found she could barely remember a single song on the piano.
words.etym: From Greek atrophia, “lack of food, wasting away”: a (without) + trophe (nourishment).

mn.text: Grandpa Gus won a tennis trophy long ago, but he hasn’t touched a racket since. The trophy gathers dust, and his tennis skills {atrophy}.

scene.alt: A grandfather dozes on the sofa beside an old, dusty trophy and a racket he never uses.

after.cap: Four ways to grow and six ways to shrink.

after.html: The moon waxes (grows) and wanes (shrinks); the tide flows in and ebbs out. Abate is the word for storms, noise, pain and anger that ease. And atrophy is shrinking for one reason only: lack of use.

opts.s: By the time the guests left, our tall pile of cookies had {dwindled} to three broken pieces.
opts.why: A pile that shrinks little by little until little is left has dwindled.

items.q: True or false: when the moon wanes, it looks bigger each night.
items.why: False. The moon waxes (grows) and then wanes (shrinks).

items.q: Which word describes a muscle that weakens because it is never used?
items.why: To atrophy is to waste away from lack of use.

items.q: We waited in the car until the hailstorm ______. Which word fits?
items.why: Storms abate, or ease. The other words describe growing.

items.q: Which word means to multiply quickly in number?
items.why: To proliferate is to multiply. Subside, ebb and wane all describe shrinking or easing.

items.q: Type the three-letter verb for the tide flowing back out to sea.
items.why: The tide flows in and ebbs out.
